newsitem.title: USA: Intel Q2 hurt by European weakness, other factors.
newsitem.headline: Intel Q2 hurt by European weakness, other factors.

text.p: Intel Corp Tuesday reported higher than expected second quarter results, but the company said revenue and earnings were down from the first quarter due to a combination of weakness in Europe, an inventory correction following a strong first quarter and product transitions in the PC industry.

Intel said net income for the three months ended June 28 totaled $1.6 billion, up 58 percent from second quarter 1996 net income of $1.0 billion, but down 17 percent from first quarter 1997 net income of $2.0 billion.
Earnings per share in the second quarter rose to $0.92 from $0.59 in the year ago quarter.
According to First Call, analysts expected Intel to report a profit of $0.90 a share.
Second quarter revenue was $6.0 billion, up 29 percent from $4.6 billion for the second quarter of 1996, but down 7.6 percent from first quarter 1997 revenue of $6.4 billion.

"Strong microprocessor shipments in the first quarter led to some inventory correction in the second quarter as the industry prepared for a rapid transition to processors with MMX technology," said Andrew Grove, chairman and chief executive officer.
"Demand for the Pentium processor with MMX technology and the Pentium II processor is strong, and we are ramping production at a record rate," he said.
During the second quarter, the company repurchased a total of 13.0 million shares of common stock at a cost of $945 million under an ongoing program.
Since the program began in 1990, the company has repurchased 198.2 million shares at a total cost of $5.6 billion.
